category.wavefront.own_voice.description: The volume of your own voice

quality.performance.tip: Lightest. 100 rays, 1 diffraction route out to 24 blocks. For slower computers.
quality.balanced.tip: In between. 200 rays, 3 diffraction routes out to 32 blocks.
quality.realism.tip: Most thorough values that still make an audible difference, and the default. 500 rays, 4 diffraction routes out to 64 blocks, 2 echoes out to 96 blocks, sounds re-checked 5 times a second.
quality.overkill.tip: Every accuracy setting at its limit, whether or not you can hear the difference: 2000 rays reaching 16 chunks, every sound re-checked every tick, 4 diffraction routes with the deepest search, 3 echoes out to 128 blocks including off rough surfaces, music and loops echo, no range or sound-count limits. Strengths stay at their real-world value of 1.0. Very heavy: expect stutter even on a fast computer.
quality.custom.tip: Your own values. Changing any setting while on a preset switches here, starting from that preset's values.

walls.title: Walls
walls.summary: How much blocks muffle sound, by material.
walls.summary_off: Sound Physics is off: using the classic method.

diffraction.summary_off: Blocked sounds are only heard through walls.

distance.summary_off: Sounds arrive instantly, as in vanilla.

water.summary_off: Water and lava are treated as air.

reverb.summary: Echo that matches the space you are in.

general.title: General
general.summary: Update speed, range, volume and tools.
general.summary_off: Update speed, range, volume and tools.

hint.preset: %s preset. Changing a setting switches Quality to Custom, starting from these values.
hint.custom: Custom: your own values. Hover a setting to see what it does to realism and performance.

prompt.title: Switch to Custom?
prompt.body: Quality is set to %s, which is a fixed preset. Changing the setting '%s' switches Quality to Custom. Custom will start with that preset's values, plus this change.

section.classic: Classic mode (only used when Sound Physics is off)

advanced.group.classic: Classic Mode (only used when Sound Physics is off)

wavefront:config.raysCast.description:
How many invisible rays are fired from you to measure the space around you. They work out how big and echoey the place is. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: more rays give a steadier, more accurate measurement, so reverb does not flutter. Most realistic: 500; more adds little.

Performance: cost grows directly with this number. Fastest: 100. Below about 50 the reverb becomes jumpy.
wavefront:config.raysBounced.description:
How many times each ray bounces off walls before it stops. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: more bounces explore side passages, but the reverb was tuned at 3 and higher values mostly make it stronger, not more accurate. Most realistic: 3.

Performance: each bounce is another ray segment for every ray. Fastest: 2.
wavefront:config.maxRayLength.description:
How far each ray travels before giving up, in chunks (16 blocks each). Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: long enough to reach the walls of the space you are in. Most realistic: 4 chunks; raise it only for caverns more than 64 blocks across.

Performance: longer rays take longer to trace in open spaces. Fastest: 3 chunks.
wavefront:config.procRange.description:
Sounds further away than this are left exactly as vanilla Minecraft plays them. -1 means no limit.

Realism: anything audible should be processed. Most realistic: 200 blocks, which already covers every sound loud enough to hear.

Performance: a smaller range means fewer sounds to work on. Fastest: about 32 blocks.
wavefront:config.tickRate.description:
How often a sound that is still playing gets re-checked, in game ticks (20 ticks = 1 second). Lower = more often. 0 = never re-check. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: more frequent checks follow you and moving sounds more closely. Most realistic: 4 ticks. Going lower adds little, because volume and position already glide between checks.

Performance: every check re-does the work for each playing sound, and it can cause stutter when many sounds play. Fastest: 10 ticks or more.
wavefront:config.soundMult.description: 1 is just default Minecraft sound dist\nPERFORMANCE IMPACT: HIGH
wavefront:config.volumeMultiplier.description:
Makes every processed sound louder or quieter.

Realism: 1x keeps the game's own volumes. Most realistic: 1x.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.reverb.description:
Adds echo that matches the space you are in: none in an open field, a long tail in a big cave.

Realism: ON, real spaces always have some. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON adds a second set of rays every time the space is measured. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.permeation.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). The original method of muffling sound through walls.

Realism: less realistic than Sound Physics, which replaces it. Within Classic mode, most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON adds wall checks for every ray. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.permeationStepSize.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). How finely the original method measures wall thickness.

Realism: smaller steps measure thickness more accurately. Most realistic: 0.0625 blocks.

Performance: smaller steps are slower. Fastest: 0.5 blocks.
wavefront:config.permeatedTickRate.description:
How often permeated sounds' positions should be updated
(0 is off)
(1 = every tick -> 20 = every second)
PERFORMANCE IMPACT: MEDIUM (higher than normal tickrate)
wavefront:config.attenuationType.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). How sound fades with distance in the original method.

Realism: none of the options follows real acoustics exactly; the original author recommends Vercidium Linear.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.rayBounce.description: Larger = less heavily the sound will be coming from walls (will make likely make sounds quieter)\nPERFORMANCE IMPACT: NONE
wavefront:config.debug.description:
Shows each processed sound's name on screen. With Sound Physics ON it also shows its volume factor, treble factor and path length. Known issue from the original mod: Chat mode can crash with Sodium.

Realism: no effect on sound.

Performance: a small cost per sound. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.maxBlocksPermeated.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). Sound stops completely after passing through this many blocks.

Realism: tuned by ear by the original author; there is no physically correct value. Suggested: 3 blocks.

Performance: a lower value ends wall checks sooner. Fastest: 1 block.
wavefront:config.permeationAbsorption.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). Volume is multiplied by this for every block of wall. Lower = walls block more.

Realism: tuned by ear by the original author; there is no physically correct value. Suggested: 0.4.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.barrierAsAir.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). Invisible barrier blocks do not muffle sound. Sound Physics always ignores barriers.

Realism: ON, an invisible block should not be heard. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.shortcutDirectionality.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). If nothing is between you and a sound, use its true direction instead of the ray-traced one.

Realism: ON, a sound in plain view should come from where it is. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.maxSounds.description:
The most sounds the mod will work on at once. Sounds beyond this play as vanilla.

Realism: high enough that nothing is skipped. Most realistic: 100, which is rarely reached.

Performance: a lower cap limits the worst case in busy places such as mob farms. Fastest: about 30.
wavefront:config.bounceAbsorptionMultiplier.description:
How much sound survives each bounce off a wall when the space is measured. 1.0 = nothing lost, 0.5 = half lost per bounce.

Realism: tuned by ear by the original author together with the other reverb values. Suggested: 0.9.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.disableFXOnUI.description:
Leaves button clicks and other menu sounds untouched. Some mods play world sounds in the same group, and those would be skipped too.

Realism: OFF processes everything. Most realistic: OFF.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.reverbTuning.description:
Shows the measured reverb values on screen, for tuning.

Realism: no effect on sound.

Performance: a small cost while it is on. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.useExplosionResistance.description:
Classic mode only (used when Sound Physics is OFF). Guesses how much a block muffles sound from how blast-proof it is.

Realism: a rough guess, but better than treating every block the same. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.legacyReverb.description:
Which version of the original mod's reverb calculation to use.

Realism: Modern is the newest and uses room size, surfaces and openness. Most realistic: Modern.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.experimentalReverb.description:
When ON, Minecraft's own distance fall-off is applied to each sound's apparent position.

Realism: ON, so a sound that reached you by a longer route is quieter. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.globalReverbIntensity.description:
Overall reverb intensity multiplier
Higher = more intense reverb

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 2.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 2.0 (the default).

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.0 (the default).

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.airAbsorptionRate.description:
How quickly air absorbs sound
Higher = more muffled distant sounds

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.003 (the default).

Minimum air absorption factor

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.1 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.roomVolumeMultiplier.description:
Room volume estimation factor
Higher = treats rooms as larger

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.7 (the default).

Surface area calculation (6 sides)

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 6.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.roomComplexityDivisor.description:
Surface/volume complexity factor
Lower = treats rooms as more complex

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 2.0 (the default).

Late reverb delay vs early reflections
Higher = later late reverb

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 1.5 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.soundSpeed.description:
Speed of sound

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 343.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.baseReverbGain.description:
Minimum reverb gain
Higher = always some reverb present

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.1 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.reverbGainMultiplier.description:
How much reverb strength affects final gain
Higher = more responsive to reverb conditions

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.4 (the default).

wavefront:config.maxOverallGain.description:
Maximum overall reverb gain
Prevents reverb from being too loud

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 1 (the default).

wavefront:config.sendFilterHfReduction.description:
High frequency reduction for send filter
Lower = more muffled reverb

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.7 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.minDiffusion.description:
Minimum reverb diffusion

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.3 (the default).

Higher = more scattered reflections

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.95 (the default).

wavefront:config.minDensity.description:
Minimum reverb density

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.3 (the default).

wavefront:config.densityRoomSizeFactor.description:
How room size affects density

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 100.0 (the default).

How absorption affects low frequency

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 3 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.decayLfMultiplier.description:
Low frequency decay ratio multiplier
Higher = longer low frequency decay

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 1.2 (the default).

wavefront:config.outdoorHfLeak.description:
High frequency leak for outdoor spaces
Higher = less muffled outdoor sound

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.7 (the default).

wavefront:config.echoTimeMultiplier.description:
Echo time based on room size
Higher = longer echo times

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.002 (the default).

wavefront:config.echoDepthMultiplier.description:
Echo depth based on density
Higher = more pronounced echoes

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.1 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.modulationTimeMultiplier.description:
Modulation time based on room size
Higher = slower modulation

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.01 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.modulationDepthMultiplier.description:
Modulation depth based on enclosure
Higher = more modulation

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.1 (the default).

wavefront:config.baseHfReference.description:
Base high frequency reference (Hz)
Higher = affects higher frequencies

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 5000.0 (the default).

wavefront:config.hfRoomSizeFactor.description:
How room size affects HF reference
Higher = more room size influence

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 20.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.baseLfReference.description:
Base low frequency reference (Hz)

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 250.0 (the default).

wavefront:config.lfRoomSizeFactor.description:

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 2.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.roomRolloffSizeFactor.description:
How room size affects rolloff
Higher = less room size influence on rolloff

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 50.0 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.rt60SabineConstant.description:
Sabine's RT60 formula constant
Physics constant - usually don't change

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.161 (the default).

wavefront:config.minTotalAbsorption.description:
Minimum absorption to prevent division by zero

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 0.1 (the default).

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.diffusionComplexityWeight.description:
Weight of room complexity in diffusion calculation
Higher = complexity affects diffusion more

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 1.0 (the default).

wavefront:config.diffusionEnclosureWeight.description:
Weight of enclosure in diffusion calculation
Higher = enclosure affects diffusion more

Realism: one of the reverb's fine-tuning values. It was set by ear by the original author and has no single physically correct value. Suggested: 1.0 (the default).

wavefront:config.diffusionReverbWeight.description:
Weight of reverb strength in diffusion calculation

wavefront:config.soundBlacklist.description:
Sounds whose name contains any of these words are played exactly as vanilla. Part of a name is enough, for example 'rain'.

Realism: every listed sound loses its physics. Most realistic: empty.

Performance: each listed sound is one less to work on.
wavefront:config.soundTickBlacklist.description:
Sounds whose name contains any of these words are processed once when they start and never updated afterwards.

Realism: listed sounds stop following you as you move. Most realistic: empty.

Performance: each listed sound saves its repeat checks.
wavefront:config.voicechatReverb.description:
Other players' voices echo to match the space, like game sounds do.

Realism: ON. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON adds a small cost per speaking player. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.voicechatReverbSelf.description:
Plays your own voice back to you with the room's echo.

Realism: in real life you do hear your own echo, so ON is closer to reality. It is OFF by default because this feature comes from the original mod and has not been tested here.

Performance: ON adds a small cost while you talk. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.voicechatMuffle.description:
Walls dull other players' voices, and voices diffract round corners and through doorways. Needs Simple Voice Chat.

Realism: ON, voices are sound like any other. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON re-checks each speaking player four times a second. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.voicechatMuffleVolume.description:
Walls make voices quieter as well as duller.

Realism: ON, real walls do both. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.wavePhysics.description:
The main switch. When ON, walls muffle sound according to what they are made of, and sound diffracts (bends) round corners and through openings.

Realism: ON uses the researched block table and diffraction. OFF falls back to the simpler Classic method. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON does extra work for each sound that is behind something. It has not been measured against Classic mode yet, so there is no 'fastest' recommendation.
wavefront:config.wallStrength.description:
How much walls block sound. Higher = walls block more. 0 = walls block nothing.

Realism: 1.0 uses the researched values for each material; a stone block then takes off about 35 dB, so a mob behind one block is very faint. Lower values make walls leakier than real ones, higher values exaggerate them. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.diffraction.description:
Diffraction is sound bending round edges and through openings. With it ON, a blocked sound reaches you round the obstacle, quieter and duller, and seems to come from the edge or gap.

Realism: ON. Without it a sound behind a free-standing wall is almost muted, which is wrong. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: ON searches for routes round the obstacle for each blocked sound. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.diffractionStrength.description:
How much quieter sound gets when it diffracts round an edge. Higher = edges cut more sound. 0 = diffraction costs nothing.

Realism: 1.0 follows the standard real-world barrier formula, where high notes lose more than low notes. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.diffractionRoutes.description:
How many different ways round an obstacle are added together for each sound. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: more routes let a sound arrive over the top and round each side, as it really does. Most realistic: 4.

Performance: every extra route is another search for each blocked sound. Fastest: 1.
wavefront:config.diffractionRange.description:
Sounds further away than this are not checked for diffraction; they only get the through-the-wall sound. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: a larger range means no audible sound is left out. Most realistic: 64 blocks.

Performance: a larger range means more and longer searches. Fastest: 24 blocks or less.
wavefront:config.diffractionSearchBudget.description:
How hard the mod looks for a route round an obstacle before giving up. Only used when Quality is set to Custom.

Realism: higher finds routes through longer, twistier tunnels. Most realistic: 12000; going higher rarely finds anything more.

Performance: this is the most work one sealed-in sound can cost. Fastest: 3000 or less.
wavefront:config.qualityPreset.description:
One switch for how much work the mod does. It sets everything on the Performance tab at once.

Realism: the Realism preset is the most thorough (500 rays, 3 bounces, sounds re-checked every 4 ticks, 4 diffraction routes out to 64 blocks). Most realistic: Realism, which is the default.

Performance: the Performance preset is the lightest (100 rays, 2 bounces, sounds re-checked every 10 ticks, 1 diffraction route out to 24 blocks). Fastest: Performance. If the game stutters when many sounds play, try Balanced (200 rays, 3 bounces, sounds re-checked every 10 ticks, 3 diffraction routes out to 32 blocks).

Custom uses the values you set on the Performance tab.
wavefront:config.openingSize.description:
Makes the size of an opening matter. A doorway or small hole only passes the sound that lands on it, then spreads it out on the far side, so a narrow gap lets less through than a wide one. Long passages are left alone, because their walls guide sound along.

Realism: ON. Without it a one-block hole passes as much as an open archway. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: a small extra check for each route that bends through an opening. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.soundDelay.description:
Sound takes time to arrive: 343 blocks per second, so a sound 34 blocks away is heard a tenth of a second late. Each sound starts at an exact moment on the audio device's clock. That also lets two sources playing the same sound at the same instant reinforce and cancel each other depending on where you stand.

Realism: ON. Most realistic: ON. Every processed sound also starts 0.03 seconds later than before, which is what makes the exact timing possible.

Performance: no effect. Needs an audio device that supports timed starts; where it does not, sounds start as before and the debug readout says so.
wavefront:config.airAbsorptionStrength.description:
Air soaks up high notes over distance, so far-off sounds are duller. 0 turns it off.

Realism: 1.0 is real air at 20 degrees and 50 percent humidity. Over 64 blocks that takes about 7 dB off the very highest notes and almost nothing off the rest, so the effect is subtle at Minecraft distances. Higher values exaggerate it. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.doppler.description:
Pitch rises as you and a sound approach each other and falls as you move apart, like a siren passing.

Realism: ON. The shift is small on foot (about 1.5 percent at a sprint) and clear when flying with an elytra or falling. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.dopplerStrength.description:
How strong the pitch shift is. 0 turns it off.

Realism: 1.0 is the real amount for the speed of sound in air. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.echoes.description:
A clear repeat of a sound off a large flat surface, such as a built wall or a sheer cliff face. The surface must be flat, at least 5 blocks across and far enough away that the repeat arrives 0.05 seconds or more after the sound; closer than that it blends into the reverb. Needs Speed of Sound to be ON. Music, looping sounds and uneven surfaces are covered by the next two settings.

Realism: ON. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: each echo is an extra copy of the sound, and each new sound checks six directions for a surface. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.echoStrength.description:
How loud echoes are. 0 silences them.

Realism: 1.0 is the real amount: an echo is quieter than the sound in proportion to how much further it travelled, less what the surface absorbs. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.echoCount.description:
The most echoes one sound can have. The strongest are kept.

Realism: in a canyon or a large hall a sound can return off two or three faces. Most realistic: 2; a third is rarely loud enough to notice.

Performance: each echo uses one more sound channel. Fastest: 1.
wavefront:config.echoRange.description:
How far away a surface can be and still be checked for an echo.

Realism: at 96 blocks an echo returns just over half a second late and is very faint; beyond that little is audible. Most realistic: 96 blocks.

Performance: longer checks reach further through the world. Fastest: 48 blocks or less.
wavefront:config.echoContinuous.description:
Gives music discs and looping sounds echoes as well. Each echo is a second copy of the sound that plays for as long as the sound does and is re-aimed as you move. Looping sounds, such as a moving minecart, pick up new surfaces as they go and drop the ones they leave behind. A music disc only echoes off surfaces that were in range when it started.

Realism: ON, a jukebox near a cliff should echo like anything else. Most realistic: ON.

Performance: each echo of a music disc is another music stream, and Minecraft only has 8 of those. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.echoRough.description:
Lets uneven surfaces echo as well as flat ones: natural cliffs, cave walls, anything whose face varies by up to 2 blocks in depth and covers at least 40 percent of a 5 by 5 patch. The rougher and patchier the surface, the weaker the echo, and high notes lose the most.

Realism: mixed. A real rough wall sends back a repeat smeared over a few hundredths of a second, and this plays one clean repeat. Against a cliff in the open that is closer to reality than no echo at all; in a rough cave it can make echoes clearer than they should be. Only the Overkill preset switches it on.

Performance: about five times as many block checks for each surface. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.water.description:
Treats water and lava as their own kind of space for sound. Sound moves about four times faster in water, very little of it crosses the surface, and with your head under you hear less treble and can hardly tell left from right. Lava works the same way with its own figures.

Realism: ON. Most realistic: ON. Real water does not make sound carry further at Minecraft distances, so that is not simulated.

Performance: a path that touches water or lava is checked every quarter block along the way; paths through air alone cost nothing extra. Fastest: OFF.
wavefront:config.waterSurfaceStrength.description:
How much is lost each time sound crosses between air and water, or air and lava. 0 lets everything through.

Realism: 1.0 is the real figure, about 29 dB for water and 36 dB for lava, so a mob on the shore is very faint from under water. That is the loss for sound hitting the surface straight on. At a slant real water lets even less through, which is not simulated. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.submergedHearing.description:
How much treble you lose while your head is under water or lava. 0 leaves your hearing unchanged.

Realism: under water people hear through the bones of the skull, and measured hearing is best around 500 to 1000 Hz instead of 3000 to 4000 Hz. 1.0 takes about 12 dB off the high notes to match. That amount is an estimate from those measurements. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.submergedDirection.description:
How much harder it is to tell left from right with your head under water. Sounds are moved towards the middle. 0 keeps full direction, as in air.

Realism: 1.0 is the real amount. Sound is about four times faster in water, so the tiny gap between it reaching one ear and the other shrinks to about a quarter, and the head stops shadowing the far ear. A sound directly to your side seems only about 14 degrees off centre. Most realistic: 1.0.

Performance: no effect.
wavefront:config.searchTimeMs.description:
How many thousandths of a second each round of calculations may spend looking for ways round obstacles. When it runs out, sounds already playing keep their last values until the next round, and a new sound starts with only its through-the-wall part and catches up a moment later. The game itself never waits for these calculations.

Realism: more time means fewer sounds have to wait a round. Most realistic: 50, about one game tick; Overkill uses 250.

Performance: this is a ceiling on how late a new sound can start when many blocked sounds play at once. Fastest: 10.
